## Why the model does this

The raw DB rules out any pipeline corruption — the string is stored exactly as the model streamed it, in one settled text block:

- `agent_message 019ff9fc…` (Coordinator, model **fable-5**): block `:1` is literally `"<group:Wrapping up</group:>\n"`, followed by tool_use blocks, then closing prose. No matching close tag anywhere later.
- `agent_message 019ff841…` (same model/specialist): `"<group:Checking review</group:>\n"`, same pattern.

So this is a token-level slip by fable-5: it starts an **open** tag (`<group:Name`) and completes it with the **close-tag suffix** (`</group:>`) instead of `>`. It's plausibly primed by the specialist instructions, which document the `</group:Name>` closing variant — after emitting a group name, the close-suffix token sequence is highly probable. It's rare (2 genuine instances in the whole DB, both from Coordinator turn-openers like "Wrapping up"/"Checking review"), which is why it slipped past the earlier fixes — those addressed streaming partial tags and other malformed shapes, not this fused one.

One nuance the raw data settled: in every genuine instance the model **meant to open a group** (tools follow immediately). So I've updated the task: the parser should treat the fused `<group:Name</group:>` as a single open tag — grouping the subsequent blocks as intended — rather than open-then-immediately-close, plus accept standalone `</group:>` as a close. Prompt-tweaking the specialist to avoid priming would be marginal; parser leniency is the durable fix.

(One known limitation worth flagging: the parser runs on raw text and ignores code spans, so a message that *quotes* these tag strings — like my own analysis message, which showed up as the third DB hit — gets its quoted tags consumed. That's pre-existing and out of scope.)

The spec and task are updated. Please review and approve the plan, and I'll delegate the fix.
